textbookText: Fig: 2.4.10 Different stages of direct lateral conjugation in Spirogyra Germination of zygospore The zygospores are thick walled diploid resting spores of Spirogyra. The zygospores are released by destruction and decay of female cell of filament. It has three layered wall and resistant to unfavourable environmental condition. On return of suitable condition, the nucleus of zygospore divides meiotically to form four haploid nuclei. Out of four haploid nuclei, three nuclei degenerate and only one becomes functional. During germination, outer wall of spore absorbs water swells up and bursts, exposing inner layer as cylindrical germ tube. The germ tube divides transversally to form two celled structure. Lower cell acts as rhizoidal cell or holdfast that attached to substratum while upper cell divides repeatedly to form new filament. The filament gets detached from the substratum and becomes a free floating Spirogyra.
Fig: 2.4.11 Different stages of germination of zygospore in Spirogyra 2.4.5 ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE OF ALGAE Algae have both positive and negative effect as mentioned below: Useful activities:

1. Food: Algal species are becoming a popular food to the mankind because of its high nutritive value and more yield per unit area than conventional crops. Algae which are commonly used as food are: Chlorella, Porphyra, Codium, Rhodymenia,etc.
2. Fooder: Many algae become popular as fodder due to their vitamin and micronutrient in addition to their carbohydrate and protein content. The fat content of milk becomes

increased with the addition of sea algae as fodder. Algae commonly used as fodder are
Fucus, Laminaria, Alaria, Ascophyllum, etc.
3. Pisciculture: Both floating and attached forms provide the primary food for fish and
other aquatic animals. Species of the green algae, the diatoms and some blue-greens are
most widely eaten up by the fishes.
4. Industry: Algae has been used to develop many products of commercial and
pharmaceutical importance. Agar-agar obtained from Gelidium species are used in
processed cheese, jam, jellies, tissue culture
media etc. Carrageenan obtained from the

cell wall of Gigartina stellate and Chondrus coagulate blood, cure cough and also use as a component of deodorants, cosmetics, toothpastes, etc. Chlorellin, an antibiotic is extracted from Chlorella. Various alga are rich source of iodine.
Some species of Chlorella like Chlorella vulgaris can be used as a source of nutrition and oxygen by astronauts in space.
5. Treatment of sewage plant: Algae produce oxygen
through the process of photosynthesis, which helps in the rapid decomposition of
sewage.
Harmful Effects Some species of algae can be toxic to the environment. Some harmful effects are described below:

1. Toxicity and parasitism: Gymnodinium veneficum, Prymnesium parvum and other species may cause mortality in fish and in domestic animals that drinks water infested with these algae. Cephaleuros species of green algae cause ‘red rust in tea’ and cause heavy economic losses by seriously affecting the yield of tea.
2. Fouling of ships: Some algae like Ulva, Enteromopha etc. are attached to the ship, and this is called fouling of ship. The fouling decreases the speed of the ship.
3. Contamination of water supply: Some algae contaminate the reservoirs of water supply of city that develops a foul odour in the water and makes the water unhygienic.
